content: Simulate a moderately dense debris flow with shear-thinning non-Newtonian material, please refer to Case4.png for geometry. Use debris density of 1600 kg/m^3, initial particle spacing dp = 0.0064 m, use Symplectic step algorithm, artificial viscosity 0.1, output time interval 0.2s and run to total time 8s.

================================================================
  SIMULATION PLAN
================================================================

### Reasoning
I treated this as a 2D debris-flow flume because the sketch shows a side profile with no lateral variation. The geometry reproduces a 23 degree inclined upstream reach transitioning into a horizontal deposition basin, with an upstream debris block of about 0.2 x 1.5 m placed on the slope and a downstream debris block of about 0.2 x 3.0 m on the flat bed, plus short retaining walls visible in the sketch. I used dp=0.0064 as requested and selected a shear-thinning Herschel-Bulkley-Papanastasiou material consistent with a moderately dense debris flow: density 1600 kg/m^3, moderate consistency, moderate yield stress, and HBP_n=0.75 for shear-thinning behavior. Artificial viscosity is set to 0.1 as requested, CFL to 0.2 for a stable but efficient run, and output/time limits match the requested 0.2 s and 8 s. The Symplectic algorithm request is execution-side rather than geometry/parameter-block side, so it should be set in the main DualSPHysics execution configuration outside this JSON block.

### Geometry XML
```xml
<geometry>
  <definition dp="0.0064">
    <pointmin x="-0.40" y="0" z="-0.20" />
    <pointmax x="4.60" y="0" z="1.80" />
  </definition>
  <commands>
    <mainlist>
      <setshapemode>dp | bound</setshapemode>
      <setdrawmode mode="full" />

      <!-- Upstream debris wedge on 23 deg slope: 0.2 x 1.5 m -->
      <setmkfluid mk="0" />
      <drawprism mask="0">
        <point x="0.00" y="-1" z="0.00" />
        <point x="1.50" y="-1" z="0.00" />
        <point x="1.50" y="-1" z="0.20" />
        <point x="0.00" y="-1" z="0.20" />
        <point x="0.00" y="1" z="0.00" />
        <point x="1.50" y="1" z="0.00" />
        <point x="1.50" y="1" z="0.20" />
        <point x="0.00" y="1" z="0.20" />
      </drawprism>
      <move x="0.45" y="0" z="0.55" />
      <rotate angx="0" angy="-23" angz="0" />
      <drawprism mask="0">
        <point x="0.00" y="-1" z="0.00" />
        <point x="1.50" y="-1" z="0.00" />
        <point x="1.50" y="-1" z="0.20" />
        <point x="0.00" y="-1" z="0.20" />
        <point x="0.00" y="1" z="0.00" />
        <point x="1.50" y="1" z="0.00" />
        <point x="1.50" y="1" z="0.20" />
        <point x="0.00" y="1" z="0.20" />
      </drawprism>
      <matrixreset />

      <!-- Downstream debris deposit: 0.2 x 3.0 m -->
      <drawbox>
        <boxfill>solid</boxfill>
        <point x="2.20" y="-1" z="0.00" />
        <size x="3.00" y="2" z="0.20" />
      </drawbox>

      <!-- Channel / flume boundaries drawn after fluid -->
      <setmkbound mk="0" />

      <!-- Sloping reach and transition using beach profile -->
      <drawbeach mask="1|2">
        <point x="-0.10" y="1" z="0.55" />
        <point x="2.20" y="1" z="0.00" />
        <point x="5.40" y="1" z="0.00" />
        <point x="5.40" y="1" z="-0.0256" />
        <point x="2.20" y="1" z="-0.0256" />
        <point x="-0.10" y="1" z="0.5244" />
      </drawbeach>

      <!-- Upstream stopper behind upper debris block -->
      <drawbox>
        <boxfill>solid</boxfill>
        <point x="0.33" y="-1" z="0.48" />
        <size x="0.0256" y="2" z="0.32" />
      </drawbox>

      <!-- Final right retaining wall -->
      <drawbox>
        <boxfill>solid</boxfill>
        <point x="5.17" y="-1" z="0.00" />
        <size x="0.0256" y="2" z="0.28" />
      </drawbox>

      <shapeout file="" />
    </mainlist>
  </commands>
</geometry>
```

### Physics Parameters
  gravity_z            = -9.81
  rhop0                = 1600.0
  coefh                = 1.0
  cflnumber            = 0.2
  phase_rhop           = 1600.0
  visco_nn             = 0.12
  tau_yield            = 0.02
  HBP_m                = 20.0
  HBP_n                = 0.75
  Visco                = 0.1
  DensityDT            = 3
  DensityDTvalue       = 0.1
  TimeMax              = 8.0
  TimeOut              = 0.2

The geometry has several structural errors. Fix all of them.  1. The slope is at the wrong angle. The channel surface currently drops 0.55 m    over 2.30 m horizontally, which is 13.4 degrees. It must be 23 degrees.  2. The upstream debris block is hollow — only its outline exists, about 1100    particles where a solid 1.5 x 0.2 m block at dp = 0.0064 needs roughly 7300.    Make it a solid, completely filled body of fluid particles.  3. There are two upstream debris blocks. One is drawn before the move and    rotation and is left lying unrotated and detached below the channel. Delete    it. Keep exactly one debris block on the slope.  4. That block must rest on the channel surface: its underside on the surface,    its 0.2 m thickness measured perpendicular to the surface and extending away    from it, and its downslope face 1.5 m from the slope toe measured along the    surface. It currently crosses through the channel.  5. The domain clips the geometry. pointmax x = 4.60 cuts the downstream debris    bed from 3.0 m to 2.39 m and deletes the retaining wall at x = 5.17    entirely. Enlarge the definition domain so it fully contains every shape you    draw, with margin on all sides.  6. The downstream section has no pool. It is a bare flat plate with no side    wall, and the debris bed sits on top of it. Build a container: a floor, a    left wall whose top is level with the slope toe, and a right wall, with the    3.0 x 0.2 m debris bed lying inside it and its top surface level with the    slope toe.  7. The channel and pool boundaries are single particle layers — two thin skins    0.026 m apart with a void between them. Make every boundary surface three    particle layers thick, grown away from the fluid, with no void.  8. Remove the small vertical block at x = 0.33. There is no gate or stopper in    the sketch.  Unchanged: 2D, dp = 0.0064, debris density 1600, and the two debris bodies at 1.5 x 0.2 m and 3.0 x 0.2 m.

1. The slope channel is rotated about the origin, but it is drawn extending from    x = -0.20 to x = +2.39 before the rotation. Rotating that about the origin    swings its lower end down to z = -0.93 — 0.93 m below the pool floor and far    below the domain floor at z = -0.20 — so about 90 percent of the channel has    been clipped away and only a fragment survives between x = -0.19 and x = 0.42.    Rebuild the channel so its lower end (the toe) sits at the centre of rotation    and the channel extends uphill from there, in the negative x direction. The toe    must end up at the top of the pool's left wall. Build the debris block the same    way so it lands on the channel surface — it is currently floating 0.64 m above    it, and its downslope face must be 1.5 m from the toe measured along the surface.  2. The pool's left wall spans z = -0.200 to -0.002, entirely below the top of the    pool floor, so it retains nothing. It must rise 0.2 m above the floor, with its    top level with the slope toe and with the top surface of the debris bed.  3. The pool's right wall rises only 0.083 m above the floor while the bed is 0.2 m    deep. Make it 0.4 m tall measured from the floor.
